Notes on practical quantum computing with Qiskit, from quantum information basics to circuits, simulators, IBM Quantum backends, and running jobs on real quantum hardware.

---

::: {.content-grid}

::: {.content-card}
**[The Math Behind Quantum Entanglement](the-math-behind-quantum-entanglement.qmd)**
A mathematical view of entanglement: Bell states, gate matrices, CNOT, and why an entangled state cannot be separated into independent single-qubit states.
:::

::: {.content-card}
**[From Zero to Quantum](from-zero-to-quantum.qmd)**
A first Qiskit workflow: install the tools, build a Bell-state hello-world circuit, run it on a simulator or IBM Quantum backend, and interpret measurement counts.
:::

::: {.content-card}
**[Qiskit Lesson 2: Multiple Systems](qiskit-lesson-2-multiple-systems.qmd)**
Compound classical and quantum systems, Cartesian products, tensor products, marginal and conditional states, CNOT, Bell states, partial measurement, and local unitary operations.
:::

::: {.content-card}
**[Qiskit Lesson 1: Classical and Quantum Information](qiskit-lesson-1-classical-and-quantum-information.qmd)**
Classical states and probability vectors, Dirac notation, deterministic and stochastic operations, quantum states as complex unit vectors, measurement, and basic qubit gates.
:::
